# WFX ERP

## Customer Specification & Approval Document
Project / Customer: Shahi Exports
Module / Functionality: KIT / Pack MRP Enhancement
Helpdesk ID: 445486
Version: [V1.0]
Date: [16-09-2026]
Prepared By: Nishant [Product Team]
Customer SPOC: [Customer Name / Designation]

## 1. Requirement & Objective
Business Requirement
We are providing a functionality to combine Styles. For example, a Sales Order contains two Packs built on the same Style — Pack 1 on Style 1 and Pack 2 on Style 1 — MRP will generate for all the Packs added into Sales Order. At MRP event Style level -1 indent will be created as a clubbed requirement against the Sales Order which will lead to create one production Order for a Style.
User visibility is provided at MRP level through two tabs — Kit Demand and MRP — so that the planner can see the KIT/Pack demand and the resulting Style and Raw Material requirement, and thereby plan the requirement more accurately.
Objective
Planning in WFX is done at Style level, not at KIT/Pack level. The objective is therefore to enhance MRP so that a KIT/Pack Sales Order is exploded down to its constituent Styles and Raw Materials, and the requirement is planned at Style level — clubbing Packs that share the same Style into a single consolidated Style requirement. Accordingly, the Production Order (PO) is raised at Style level, one per distinct Style, while the Job Order (JO) is generated for KIT/Pack.
Use Case / Business Scenario
• A KIT (KIT-364) is made up of two different Styles — Style 1 (Flannel Pants) and Style 2 (Flannel LS Shirt). Sales Order for KIT: 1,000 Qty.
• Pack 1 (KIT-366) is made up of two or more units of the same Style (Style 1 & 2 – Flannel Pants). Sales Order for Pack 1: 500 Qty.
• Pack 2 (KIT-367) is made up of two or more units of the same Style (Style 1 & 2 – Flannel Pants). Sales Order for Pack 2: 500 Qty.
• Pack 1 and Pack 2 are built on the same Style, so at the time of MRP the planner can club them together and plan a single consolidated Style requirement instead of planning each Pack separately.
• Clubbing example: if a single Sales Order contains Pack 1 on Style 1 and Pack 2 on Style 1, both Packs are clubbed and a single Production Order is generated for Style 1, covering the combined quantity of both Packs & trigger point is Run MRP.
• On the Pending MRP screen, the planner can see the KIT/Pack at Level ‑1 and drill down to the Styles (Level 1) and Raw Materials (Level 2) that the KIT/Pack will consume, giving full visibility of what is being planned before any document is raised.
• Pack: since a Pack contains two or more units of the same Style, a single Production Order is generated for that Pack.
• KIT: since KIT-364 contains two different Styles (Style 1 and Style 2), two Production Orders are generated — one per Style.
• Running MRP on the KIT/Pack directly creates the Job Order at KIT/Pack level, while the Production Orders are created at Style level.

## 2. Scope

### In Scope
• Definition of KIT and Pack as a combination of two or more Styles.
• Clubbing at MRP level: Packs built on the same Style can be clubbed at the time of MRP (Trigger Point), into a single consolidated requirement.
• Enhancement of the Pending MRP List screen for KIT and Pack Sales Orders, with two tabs: Kit Demand and MRP.
• Kit Demand tab (Level ‑1): displays KIT/Pack Sales Orders and allows same-Style Packs to be clubbed; actions taken here drive the requirement generated on the MRP tab.
• MRP tab: displays Styles (Level 1) and Raw Materials (Level 2) generated from the Kit Demand tab, giving the planner visibility of the full requirement before documents are raised.
• Job Order (JO) generation at KIT/Pack level when MRP is run — no Production Order is raised at KIT/Pack level.
• Production Order (PO) generation at Style level — one PO per distinct Style in the KIT/Pack (single PO for a Pack; multiple POs for a KIT).
• FPO generation at Style level against the clubbed requirement.
• Traceability from the Style-level requirement back to the contributing KIT/Pack Sales Orders.

### Out of Scope
• Clubbing of Packs built on different Styles.
• Changes to the existing Style-level MRP, Production Order, FPO and Job Order logic beyond what is described in this document.
Any requirement not explicitly covered under the approved scope will be treated as a change request.

## 3. Proposed Solution

### Solution Overview
WFX will enhance the Pending MRP List screen so that KIT and Pack Sales Orders are visible as demand and are exploded to Style level, where planning is actually carried out. A new Kit Demand tab will show the KIT/Pack at Level ‑1, where the planner can select and club Packs that are built on the same Style so they are planned as one consolidated requirement rather than Pack by Pack. The resulting requirement is shown on a new MRP tab, which lists the Styles that make up the selected KIT/Packs (Level 1) and the Raw Materials those Styles consume (Level 2) — giving the planner clear visibility of the full requirement before any document is raised.
The Job Order (JO) is generated at KIT/Pack level — running MRP on the KIT/Pack directly creates its Job Order. The Production Orders (PO) are generated at Style level, one per distinct Style contained in the KIT/Pack. For a Pack, which holds two or more units of the same Style, this results in a single PO. For a KIT such as KIT-364, which holds Style 1 (Flannel Pants) and Style 2 (Flannel LS Shirt), this results in two POs — one per Style. Where Packs have been clubbed, the Style-level PO carries the clubbed quantity.

### Process / Workflow
KIT/Pack build-up from Style BOMs

### Key Functional Behavior

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 9 rows · columns: # (integer), Functionality / Rule (text), Expected Behavior (text)]
| # | Functionality / Rule | Expected Behavior |
| 1 | Pending MRP List – Kit Demand tab (Level ‑1) | Displays KIT/Pack Sales Orders with defined columns; selections and actions taken here generate the requirement shown on the MRP tab. |
| 2 | Clubbing of Packs by Style | Where two or more Packs are built on the same Style, the system allows them to be clubbed and plans a single consolidated Style requirement (e.g., Pack 1 – 500 Qty and Pack 2 – 500 Qty on Flannel Pants are planned as one requirement of 1000 Qty). |
| 4 | Pending MRP List – MRP tab | Displays Styles at Level 1 (with clubbed quantity) and Raw Materials at Level 2, derived from the Kit Demand tab requirement. |
| 5 | Requirement traceability | The planner can trace a Style-level requirement back to the KIT/Pack Sales Orders that contributed to it. |
| 6 | Job Order (JO) generation – KIT/Pack level | Running MRP on the KIT/Pack directly creates the Job Order at KIT/Pack level; no Production Order is raised at this level. |
| 7 | Production Order (PO) generation – Style level | One Production Order is created per distinct Style contained in the KIT/Pack, against the clubbed Style requirement. |
| 8 | PO generation for a Pack | A Pack contains two or more units of the same Style, so a single Production Order is generated for the Pack. |
| 9 | PO generation for a KIT | A KIT contains multiple Styles (e.g., Style 1 and Style 2), so two Production Orders are generated — one per Style. |
| 10 | FPO generation | FPO is created at Style level against the clubbed Style requirement. |

### Key Validations / Business Rules
• A KIT consists of two distinct Styles (e.g., Style 1 – Flannel Pants & Style 2 – Flannel LS Shirt).
• A Pack consists of two or more units of the same Style combination (e.g., Style 1 & 2 – Flannel Pants).
• Only Packs built on the same Style may be clubbed together; Packs on different Styles cannot be combined.
• Requirement generation always flows top-down: KIT/Pack (Level ‑1) → Style (Level 1) → Raw Material (Level 2).
• Job Orders are generated at KIT/Pack level; Production Orders are generated at Style level. No Production Order is raised against the KIT/Pack itself.
• The number of Production Orders generated equals the number of distinct Styles in the KIT/Pack: one PO for a Pack (same Style), two POs for a two-Style KIT.
• Where a Sales Order contains two or more Packs built on the same Style, those Packs are clubbed and a single Production Order is generated for that Style, for the combined quantity of the clubbed Packs.
• Style-level PO and FPO quantities must reconcile to the KIT/Pack Sales Order quantity as per the KIT/Pack composition ratio.

## 4. Assumptions & Dependencies
• Style-wise BOM (Bill of Material) is already configured for each Style used in a KIT/Pack.
• KIT/Pack master mapping (which Styles and quantity ratio make up each KIT/Pack) is configured in the system.
• Sales Orders for KIT/Pack are booked with the correct Style linkage.
• [Integration dependency, if any]

## 5. Acceptance Criteria
The delivered functionality will be considered as meeting the approved specification when:
• The Pending MRP List screen shows the Kit Demand tab and MRP tab as specified.
• Packs built on the same Style can be clubbed, and the clubbed quantity is correctly reflected in the Style-level requirement.
• Actions taken on the Kit Demand tab correctly generate the requirement on the MRP tab (Style – Level 1, Raw Material – Level 2).
• The planner can trace a Style-level requirement back to the contributing KIT/Pack Sales Orders.
• Running MRP for a KIT/Pack directly creates the Job Order at KIT/Pack level, with no Production Order raised at that level.
• A Pack generates a single Production Order at Style level; a two-Style KIT generates two Production Orders, one per Style.
• A Sales Order containing two Packs on the same Style (Pack 1 – Style 1 and Pack 2 – Style 1) generates a single Production Order for Style 1 with the combined quantity.
• PO and FPO quantities reconcile to the KIT/Pack Sales Order quantities as per the composition ratio.

## 6. Approval & Sign-Off
By signing below, the customer confirms that the Requirement, Scope, Proposed Solution, Workflow, Screens/Prototype and Business Rules documented above have been reviewed and approved.
Any subsequent change or additional requirement will be evaluated and managed through the agreed Change Request / Scope Change process.
